decisive_items: Gadolinium-enhanced MRI showed enhancement confined to the peripheral rim of the mass
a 1.5 cm intra-articular space-occupying lesion invading the tibial plateau
response.rationale: The lesion's peripheral rim enhancement, intra-articular location with tibial plateau invasion, and T2 heterogeneity with internal specks are most consistent with a giant cell tumor, which commonly affects young adults and can erode into the joint. A ganglion cyst is less likely due to atypical T1 isointensity and bone invasion.

rejected.why: No mass lesion on MRI; symptoms and tenderness are nonspecific and plain films unremarkable.
Osteochondroma typically shows cortical/medullary continuity and is exophytic; plain films unremarkable and intra-articular invasion are atypical.
Synovial chondromatosis usually presents with multiple loose bodies and often calcifications on plain films; here a solitary lesion with unremarkable radiographs.
Ganglion cyst typically has fluid signal (T1 hypointense) and does not invade bone; T1 isointense to muscle and tibial plateau invasion are atypical.
